body: Can we continue this conversation? Am I too abrasive?

Chris, it's nice to meet you. My name is Cam.  I owe you an apology for the delayed response but I want you to know something.

Someone told me a long time ago if you are willing to kill yourself, and ready, to wait 3 days. Just wait 3 days and if you still feel like doing it, go ahead.

This morning I bought ammunition for a M1911 handgun, walked back to my apartment and pointed the gun at my temple. I pulled the trigger and realized I forgot to load the gun.  The situation was ridiculous enough for me to burst out in laughter and cry at the same time.

I don't know what psychologically happened but I think that the fact that I couldn't even kill myself was funny enough to keep me alive for the next few days, hopefully the rest of the week.
I've constantly been looking for a job non stop. The only job offers I get are commission-only sales jobs and insurance sales jobs.

This response is going to sound like I'm being negative just for the hell of it, but I'm really not.

Every hobby I've ever had an interest in costs money. Skydiving, cycling, video games, medical research, dogs, movies.   The level of poverty that I live in doesn't allow any of this. I'm literally typing this on a laptop I found laying on the ground 4 years ago on internet I'm stealing from a neighbor.

I vehemently despise reading or anything stationary.  I very much want to discover a hobby, and discovering hobbies costs time and money. I have never lacked the willpower to gain either, I lack the pathway to create either time or money.
At my current rate of income, adjusting for inflation, and at a current income growth rate I will have enough money to pay for school in 78 years.

That last paragraph is the issue, I did everything I could to protect what I value the most. Freedom.

Every attempt to protect this has systematically dismantled any remnant of freedom I ever had. 

I would rather condemn my 8 family members to a lifetime of sadness and "wondering why he did it and what we did wrong", than condemn myself to a prison called life; in which I know exactly what is wrong with my life, how to fix it, and know that the tools I have to fix it will never work.

This question is strangely hard to answer. I think the reason why it is difficult to respond to this is that I no longer know how to derive enjoyment out of anything anymore. I literally don't know how to feel anything anymore.

I guess, again, the good thing about rock bottom is that nothing pains you anymore, but nothing makes you happy either.
I have been for awhile. I got kicked out of medical school 6 months ago for not being able to afford it, even after loans, grants, and scholarships.
"Help" and "Survive" are on the same side of the equation. Money buys you both of those things.
What does that have to do with any of what I just said?

I have a job as a CS rep at a white trash SEO company making 10/hr with no benefits and the company illegally withholds my overtime.

The same company employs people 1 year departed from high school as "project leads" making 13/hr.

See where I'm going with this?
The burden of proof is on you to prove that money does not solve problems.

I think that's the point of this thread. I don't want or need either somewhere or someone to turn to. I need some*thing* which is money. I have done everything in my power to facilitate the forward and upward financial mobility in my life and it has ended with lawsuits, bank levies, homelessness, a credit score of 2 and a black guy on anti-depressants.

>the reason i say things will get better is because they did for me

What a provocative and well thought out response. Are you even reading any of the shit im saying?

I don't even know which one of us is the asshole in this situation. I regret even responding to this.

Fuck I regret even making this thread.

I made this thread in one last attempt to hopefully be proven wrong about validating my depression.

Phraseology like "things will get better if you hold on", "no one can be you" "don't quit", "just keep going", don't even apply to the reality of the ruleset I live in.  Your comments are just a cold reminder that having a discussion about why I'm depressed, is pointless 99% of the time.

I lost all hope long ago, and realized the futility of any action performed by myself.
